ONE_LINE: History lives on disk; RAM holds only current materialized state.

disk: the complete immutable event log -- authoritative, fully auditable by streaming
ram: a small bounded recent-event buffer if needed
TARGET_SHAPE.removed_from_ram: every historical event, indefinitely retained as Python objects

MEASUREMENT_BEFORE_ASSUMPTION.instruction_followed: Do not assume removing _events halves RSS -- measure it first.
MEASUREMENT_BEFORE_ASSUMPTION.what_the_measurement_actually_says: Removing _events reclaims ~58% of ACCOUNTED python-object memory, not a guaranteed halving of RSS: 174 MB of the 467 MB RSS is unaccounted (CPython allocator overhead and interpreter baseline) and will not move. The honest projection is a large but sub-half reduction in RSS, to be REMEASURED rather than predicted.
MEASUREMENT_BEFORE_ASSUMPTION.the_non_obvious_finding: _records shows independent=71.3 MB but marginal=5.3 MB. The ClaimRecord objects are shared with consolidation._active and the indexes, so deleting _records alone would reclaim almost nothing. Any future attempt to shrink record residency must address ALL holders together, or it will measure as a no-op.

ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A2: corpus_version remains correct without counting an in-memory history.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A3: Full genesis replay produces exactly the same state hash as before the change.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A4: Incremental state still equals independent full consolidation after every tested transition (C9 unchanged).
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A5: Retraction, contradiction and supersession semantics remain identical.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A6: Append-only log bytes remain unchanged in meaning and remain authoritative.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A7: Ingestion stays approximately O(1) per event.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A8: Retrieval results are identical before/after the optimization.
ACCEPTANCE_CONDITIONS.A10: RSS is REMEASURED at 100k, 500k and 1M rather than estimated.

A3_METHOD: State hashes for the pre-change implementation are captured from the existing 1M log at 100k/500k/1M BEFORE the change, and compared byte-for-byte afterwards. Comparing the new implementation only against itself would prove nothing.
SNAPSHOT_CAPABILITY_GAP_DOCUMENTED: Valid snapshots currently provide integrity and recovery state but NO startup acceleration -- measured: cold, snapshot-validated and snapshot-invalidated startup are equal within noise (9.6% max gap at 100k/500k/1M), because ClaimStore always replays the full log. This is a CAPABILITY GAP, not presently a scalability failure: 1M restarts in ~18s. Recorded so it is not mistaken for either a bug or a solved problem.

CHECKPOINTED_FAST_START_DEFERRED.reason: 1M -> 17.8s cold replay is not yet painful enough to justify complicating the recovery model.
CHECKPOINTED_FAST_START_DEFERRED.revisit_after: Removing historical events from RAM may reduce GC/allocation pressure enough that the observed 500k->1M replay superlinearity (2.74x time for 2x events) improves as a side effect. Restart MUST therefore be re-benchmarked after this milestone, before deciding when checkpointing becomes necessary.

Append a verification event carrying who/what checked it, evidence ids, method/version, timestamp and result; replay derives current status.
